checks.scope: BRIEF-6.md Part B only: six families x four orientations x summer/winter = 48 bridge sprites. Approved out/ files and the six named reference/road-<family>.png atlases are comparison sources only.
checks.previous_review: Compared SHA-256 values with critic-r6B-1-audit.json. All 47 previous passes are byte-for-byte unchanged and remain passed. Only the previously failed scifi-bridge-v@winter changed; its concrete defect has been rechecked and resolved. No new concrete defect was found in an inherited pass.
checks.individual_8x: Visually inspected all 48 current sprites in six family sheets at nearest-neighbour 8x. Checkerboard makes silhouette and edge clusters visible. The revised sci-fi winter vertical was additionally inspected in an 8x before/after composite. Separate checker/dark/light 8x fringe strips are saved for every sprite; these supplemental strips were not all separately opened.
checks.random_8x2_1x_4x: Visually inspected six seeded 8-column x 2-row one-cell stress sheets, assembled into all-random-8x2-1x/4x. Every family orientation/season occurs twice. No rectangular matte, unexplained cell grid, texture seam or excessive surface noise. Deliberate railing post rhythms are construction details; arbitrary mismatched orientations in this stress sheet are not valid road-join tests.
checks.road_crossings_1x_4x: Visually inspected every current file in six family crossing sheets at both 1x and 4x. Each sprite is placed in the middle cell with untransformed tiles from its actual road atlas and transparent water sides. Diagonals include the atlas spill triangles in the neighbouring cells. All 48 reach the intended edges/corners without a gap or abrupt deck hue change. Flat water colours are test backgrounds.
checks.size_width_placement: All 48 are RGBA 48x48. Straight decks are centred and run edge to edge; diagonal decks connect opposite corners. The named reference atlases have approximately 20-22px straight road widths, wider than the brief's approximate 12-14px. Bridges match the actual named reference road widths; this is accepted because narrowing them would break the required joins. Railings and end abutments remain outside the driving surface.
checks.pixel_quality: Audit confirms binary alpha (0/255), one 8-connected visible component per sprite, no exact duplicate RGBA images, and visible seasonal changes in every winter sprite. The 8x visual sheets show discrete, hard pixel clusters without blurred interpolation or antialiased contour ramps. No detached export specks, pale summer fringe or square opaque background was found.
checks.light: Upper/left post and rail accents and lower/right dark edges are compatible with the approved lighting. Cyan is emissive. No concrete reversed-light defect was found.
checks.palette_and_scale: Compared bridges at matched pixel scale with approved markers, representative round-2 city/slums/industry/suburb/farmland tiles and paddies, plus seasonal grass/plains bases and details. Inspected approved-context-summer/winter and grass/plains-season-calibration composites at 1x and 4x, and approved reference contact sheets at 1x. Restrained timber/stone/metal colours and snow highlights sit within the approved palette. Modern smooth pavement remains readable at 1x; wasteland rust is broken by grey scrap rather than becoming an orange slab.
checks.season: Every winter sprite retains a readable road and family construction with visible snow attached to deck edges or rails. None is blank or merely a duplicate of summer. The only prior failed snow placement, sci-fi vertical y=45, is removed without stripping its rail snow.
checks.near_duplicates: No pixel-identical files. All eight sprites per family were compared visually at 8x and in random sheets. Shared road palettes and rotated orientation construction are expected; timber beams, red stone-bridge rails, steel trusses, concrete guards, cyan metal and patched scrap remain distinguishable at 1x. No unjustified near-duplicate variant was found.
checks.bases_3x3: Not applicable: Part B contains no seamless bases. Four approved summer/winter grass/plains bases also have saved 3x3 tilings at 1x/4x for reference; they receive no verdict and were not used to extend review scope.
checks.peaks_range_forest_and_other_specific_fa: Not applicable to Part B: no peaks/ridges for a lattice/range composite, no trees for a forest composite, no craters, ruins, city ground bases or autumn crowns. Egg-crate peaks, Swiss-cheese craters, classical ruins, stamped cyberpunk city grids, flat orange autumn crowns and identical crowns are out of scope. All applicable bridge checks were performed.
checks.integrity: SHA-256 snapshots of all PNGs in out/ before and after review match exactly. No out/ file was written.

family_observations.fantasy: Timber crossboards, warm posts and dark joints are readable against the quiet road-colour deck; muted gold/brown fits the fantasy markers.
family_observations.wuxia: Red lacquer rails and pale stone abutments distinguish the bridge from the dirt road; the bowed railing profile gives the horizontal/diagonal sprites an arch without a separate oval shadow or opaque water backdrop.
family_observations.jazz_age: Cool riveted/braced steel rails with small warm abutments read as a truss at cell scale; they fit the cream/steel approved buildings without competing with them.
family_observations.modern: Concrete shoulders and pale guard rails frame an asphalt-colour deck. The smoother h/v/d2 surfacing is credible bridge pavement, while d1 has more scuffing; this does not introduce a colour step at the ends.
family_observations.scifi: Dark metal, sparse bolts and thin cyan accents fit the road atlas; the cyan remains restrained beside approved sci-fi markers. The d1 diagonal has rail shadows rather than a blurred gradient.
family_observations.wasteland: Grey scrap sheets, irregular rusty patches and plank/metal side supports read as repaired construction; the rust is local, with enough grey remaining to avoid a flat orange slab.
